doc.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

chapter: Opening and early jazz in England
title: American songs in Britain and wartime
summary: American standards reached England and France via cover versions, and the Glenn Miller Army Air Force Band came during the war.

bands.name: Glenn Miller Army Air Force Band

blocks.x: Did the American songwriters of the 30s and 40s, did their songs make it over to England?

Yeah, quite a few of them did. I mean a lot of them made it further than anywhere else on the continent. I mean in France you get songs like “Ces Petit Choses” which is “These Foolish Things,” you know, and I mean they sang them with French lyrics. Quite a lot of the songs found their way over there and were sung, very well sometimes, by Jean Sablon — and in England too, absolutely. I mean very often the British bands would record a cover version of an American hit and things like that. Sure. And then of course during the war when there was a lot of Americans in England as you know, service people and that, I mean they brought their music with them. Of course you had the wonderful Glenn Miller Army Air Force Band came over.
